keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; its Kingdom of Prussia and Commonwealth shapes draw the land). The page: 'In 1806 it had 914,610 inhabitants with a territory of less than 55,000 km2'; the union of gazetteer regions drawn here is about 39,000 km2 before Dobrzyń and Płock (ratio 0.7 to the infobox ceiling): within a factor of two, the shape is probably small. The Płock department and the Dobrzyń lands come from South Prussia.

ledger.note: 24 October 1795: the Third Partition gives Prussia New East Prussia. 'was a province of the Kingdom of Prussia from 1795 to 1807' (infobox: Third Partition, 24 October 1795); Prussia received 'Podlachia, the remainder of Masovia, and Warsaw' with about 1 million people (Third Partition page; Warsaw went to South Prussia). The province lay between East Prussia and the Vistula, Bug and Memel (Neman) rivers.

9 July 1807: 'The area around Białystok was ceded to the Russian Empire, becoming the Belostok Oblast' (Treaties of Tilsit).

notes:
The Prussian partition zone of 1795, a state Cliopatria lacks. Typed colony (province of kingdom-of-prussia). The gazetteer union (Podlachian voivodeship plus two radii) is a stand-in: the page names 'parts of Masovia, Podlaskie, the Trakai voivodeship and Žemaitija' without a boundary. Warsaw belongs to South Prussia in the pages opened.

Not settled: (1) the 1796 boundary with Austria's West Galicia and New Silesia (Częstochowa, Siewierz, Pilica) are not on the New East Prussia page; New Silesia (1795-1807) needs its own page and dossier. (2) The subdivisions (Kreise) are not named. (3) The area 'less than 55,000 km2' is a ceiling. (4) The month of the Dobrzyń and Płock transfer follows the Third Partition date.
